### LAE is not a mini-airline {#f01-differs}

Open in [Week 1 notes](week-01.qmd#w01-differs-svg).

```{=html}
<figure class="wdiag wdiag-svg" id="w01-differs-svg" aria-labelledby="w01-differs-svg-title">
<p class="wdiag-cap" id="w01-differs-svg-title"><strong>LAE is not a mini-airline</strong> — short-distance, high-frequency operations; an <strong>entire ecosystem</strong> (sites, charging, digital coordination, insurance, maintenance) — not only an airframe; different cost structures, operating models, and regulatory needs. <strong>Managerial implication:</strong> a fast aircraft does not automatically create a valuable *service*. Structural contrasts only — no invented Hong Kong fare data.</p>

### Nested labels, not synonyms {#f01-nested-labels}

Open in [Week 1 notes](week-01.qmd#w01-nested-labels).

```{=html}
<figure class="wdiag wdiag-svg" id="w01-nested-labels" aria-labelledby="w01-nested-labels-title">
<p class="wdiag-cap" id="w01-nested-labels-title"><strong>Nested labels, not synonyms</strong> — <strong>LAE</strong> is the umbrella; <strong>UAM</strong> is a <em>subset</em> (people or cargo over short distances inside a dense city); <strong>AAM</strong> is a broader industry label (cities to suburbs or other corridors). Keep them nested, not interchangeable. EU / US / NASA-style AAM materials are comparators, not Hong Kong law.</p>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 720 460" role="img" style="display:block;width:100%;max-width:44rem;height:auto;margin:.35rem 0 .15rem" aria-labelledby="f01-nested-labels-b2-title f01-nested-labels-b2-desc">
  <title id="f01-nested-labels-b2-title">Nested labels, not synonyms</title>
  <desc id="f01-nested-labels-b2-desc">Nested diagram. LAE is the umbrella for economic activity in low-altitude airspace plus the supporting ecosystem. UAM is a subset inside LAE: moving people or cargo over short distances inside a dense city. AAM is a broader industry label for new aircraft connecting cities to suburbs or other corridors. Keep them nested, not interchangeable. EU, US, and NASA-style AAM materials are comparators, not Hong Kong law.</desc>

  <rect x="12" y="12" width="696" height="436" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#d9d4c7" stroke-width="1"/>

  <text x="360" y="38" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui,Segoe UI,sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="700" fill="#003366">Nested labels, not synonyms</text>
  <text x="360" y="56" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui,Segoe UI,sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#5f5f5f">Keep LAE, UAM, and AAM nested — not interchangeable</text>

  <!-- AAM outer dashed ellipse — room on the right for its callout -->
  <ellipse cx="300" cy="220" rx="250" ry="125" fill="#f8f6f1" stroke="#C5A572" stroke-width="2.5" stroke-dasharray="8 5"/>

  <!-- LAE solid ellipse, inset left of AAM -->
  <ellipse cx="270" cy="230" rx="175" ry="95" fill="#e8eef5" stroke="#003366" stroke-width="2.5"/>

  <!-- UAM innermost — no text inside; leader to label below-left -->
  <ellipse cx="250" cy="235" rx="78" ry="48" fill="#F7F6F3" stroke="#003366" stroke-width="2"/>

### Four families · different binding constraints {#f01-four-families}

Open in [Week 1 notes](week-01.qmd#w01-four-families-svg).

```{=html}
<figure class="wdiag wdiag-svg" id="w01-four-families-svg" aria-labelledby="w01-four-families-svg-title">
<p class="wdiag-cap" id="w01-four-families-svg-title"><strong>Four families · different binding constraints</strong> — <strong>Cargo</strong>: time / reliability / access → payload, weather, sites, BVLOS. <strong>Passenger</strong>: door-to-door vs MTR / taxi / Airport Express → vertiport, load factor, noise, acceptance. <strong>Inspection</strong>: lower disruption vs manned access → safety case, data/privacy, repeatability. <strong>EMS / public</strong>: time-critical outcomes → priority rules, funding, acceptance. Not market-share claims. High EMS WTP ≠ unlimited pricing. Cite Use cases for examples only. Sandbox ≠ Sandbox X.</p>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" style="display:block;width:100%;max-width:44rem;height:auto;margin:.35rem 0 .15rem" viewBox="0 0 720 360" role="img" aria-labelledby="u3-title u3-desc">

Inspection: lower disruption and risk; binds on safety case, data and privacy, repeatability. Emergency and public services: outcomes alternatives cannot match in time; binds on priority rules, funding, acceptance. Not market-share claims. High willingness to pay for EMS is not unlimited pricing. Cite Use cases for examples only. Sandbox is not Sandbox X.</desc>

### Three-step viability screen {#f01-vot-npv}

Open in [Week 1 notes](week-01.qmd#w01-vot-npv-svg).

```{=html}
<figure class="wdiag wdiag-svg" id="w01-vot-npv-svg" aria-labelledby="w01-vot-npv-svg-title">
<p class="wdiag-cap" id="w01-vot-npv-svg-title"><strong>Three-step viability screen</strong> — (1) create value for customers (e.g. VOT × ΔT); (2) capture enough as operating profit (revenue − operating cost); (3) justify the initial investment (NPV). Time savings support willingness to pay, but fare, demand, costs, and investment determine financial viability. A sandbox may cut learning cost — it is <strong>not</strong> proof of NPV. Sandbox ≠ Sandbox X.</p>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 720 350" role="img" style="display:block;width:100%;max-width:44rem;height:auto;margin:.35rem 0 .15rem" aria-labelledby="g3-title g3-desc">
  <title id="g3-title">Three-step viability screen</title>
  <desc id="g3-desc">Three-step viability screen from Week 1. Step 1: does the service create value for customers, for example via value of time times time saved. Step 2: can the operator capture enough of that value as annual operating profit equals revenue minus operating cost. Step 3: does the project justify the initial investment under net present value. Time savings support willingness to pay, but fare, demand, costs, and investment determine financial viability. A sandbox may cut learning cost — it is not proof of NPV.</desc>

### Generalized cost — door-to-door {#f01-gc}

Open in [Week 1 notes](week-01.qmd#w01-gc-svg).

```{=html}
<figure class="wdiag wdiag-svg" id="w01-gc-svg" aria-labelledby="w01-gc-svg-title">
<p class="wdiag-cap" id="w01-gc-svg-title"><strong>Generalized cost — door-to-door</strong> — GC = ticket price + VOT × travel time (in-vehicle, wait, board, transfer). Prefer <strong>lower</strong> GC. A faster mode can charge more <strong>only up to</strong> the value of time saved. Design the <strong>complete journey</strong>, not only cruise time — access/wait friction can reverse the ranking. Week 4 returns to demand and mode choice.</p>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 720 370" role="img" style="display:block;width:100%;max-width:44rem;height:auto;margin:.35rem 0 .15rem" aria-labelledby="h1-title h1-desc">
  <title id="h1-title">Generalized cost — door-to-door</title>
  <desc id="h1-desc">Generalized cost equals ticket price plus value of time times travel time. Customers compare money cost, time cost, and other factors such as reliability. All else equal they prefer lower generalized cost. A faster mode can charge more only up to the value of the time saved. Design implication: plan the complete journey, not only cruise time in the air.</desc>
  <rect x="12" y="12" width="696" height="346" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#d9d4c7" stroke-width="1"/>
  <text x="360" y="34" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui,Segoe UI,sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="700" fill="#003366">Generalized cost — door-to-door</text>
  <text x="360" y="52" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui,Segoe UI,sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#5f5f5f">Money + time (and more) · not cruise minutes alone</text>

### Create value ≠ capture it — ticket HK$300 {#f01-valuechain}

Contracts and bargaining power decide the split. UTM ≠ U-space (EU frame ≠ HK law). “From 2028” Smart LATMS = planning WATCH, not city-wide UTM today. Sandbox ≠ Sandbox X.</p>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" style="display:block;width:100%;max-width:44rem;height:auto;margin:.35rem 0 .15rem" viewBox="0 0 720 360" role="img" aria-labelledby="u2-title u2-desc">

### Empty seats raise unit cost {#f01-empty-seat}

Open in [Week 1 notes](week-01.qmd#w01-empty-seat-svg).

```{=html}
<figure class="wdiag wdiag-svg" id="w01-empty-seat-svg" aria-labelledby="w01-empty-seat-svg-title">
<p class="wdiag-cap" id="w01-empty-seat-svg-title"><strong>Empty seats raise unit cost</strong> — cost per passenger = variable cost per passenger + daily fixed cost ÷ (flights per day × seats per flight × load factor). Utilization = how often it flies; load factor = share of seats filled. Need <strong>both</strong> frequent operations and sufficient demand — flying often with empty seats still leaves unit cost high. Classroom drivers only — not a Hong Kong fleet forecast.</p>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 720 360" role="img" style="display:block;width:100%;max-width:44rem;height:auto;margin:.35rem 0 .15rem" aria-labelledby="h2-title h2-desc">
  <title id="h2-title">Empty seats raise unit cost</title>
  <desc id="h2-desc">Cost per passenger equals variable cost per passenger plus daily fixed cost divided by flights per day times seats per flight times load factor. Utilization is how often the aircraft flies. Load factor is the share of seats filled. Operators need both frequent operations and sufficient demand. Flying often does not help if the aircraft repeatedly flies empty. Classroom illustration only.</desc>
  <rect x="12" y="12" width="696" height="336" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#d9d4c7" stroke-width="1"/>

  <text x="360" y="112" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui,Segoe UI,sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#003366">+ daily fixed ÷ (flights × seats × load factor)</text>

<div class="wdiag-box"><strong>Same OD / same mission?</strong><br/>Substitute services compete for the same customer trip or payload.</div>
<div class="wdiag-box"><strong>Same scarce pad / slot?</strong><br/>Rivals may compete for infrastructure even if missions differ.</div>
<div class="wdiag-box"><strong>Same corridor–time window?</strong><br/>Airspace access can bind before “market share” does (Week 8).</div>
<div class="wdiag-box fact"><strong>Discipline</strong><br/>Name the market before computing concentration. Classroom HHI shares are illustrative — not Hong Kong firm data.</div>
</div>

</details>

### Density feedback — not automatic monopoly {#f02-density}

Open in [Week 2 notes](week-02.qmd#w02-density-svg).

```{=html}
<figure class="wdiag wdiag-text" id="f02-density-text" aria-labelledby="f02-density-text-title">
<details class="wdiag-text-details">
<summary class="wdiag-text-sum">Text diagram</summary>
<p class="wdiag-cap" id="f02-density-text-title"><strong>Density feedback (conceptual)</strong></p>
<div class="wdiag-flow">
<div class="wdiag-box"><strong>More flights on shared fixed cost</strong><br/>(pad rent, staffing, coordination)</div>
<div class="wdiag-arrow" aria-hidden="true">↓</div>
<div class="wdiag-box"><strong>Lower average cost per flight</strong> (when utilization rises)</div>
<div class="wdiag-arrow" aria-hidden="true">↓</div>
<div class="wdiag-box"><strong>Stronger position at that site</strong> — if demand and permission hold</div>
<div class="wdiag-arrow" aria-hidden="true">⚠</div>
<div class="wdiag-box muted"><strong>Not automatic monopoly</strong><br/>Entry, regulation, rival pads, and congestion can reverse the advantage.</div>
</div>
<p class="wdiag-note">Schematic teaching loop — not a forecast of any Hong Kong site.</p>
</details>
</figure>
```

```{=html}
<figure class="wdiag wdiag-svg" id="w02-density-svg" aria-labelledby="w02-density-svg-title">
<p class="wdiag-cap" id="w02-density-svg-title"><strong>Density feedback — not automatic monopoly</strong> — more flights on shared fixed cost → lower average cost per flight (when utilization rises) → stronger position at that site if demand and permission hold. Entry, regulation, rival pads, and congestion can reverse the advantage. Schematic teaching loop — not a forecast of any Hong Kong site.</p>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 720 380" role="img" style="display:block;width:100%;max-width:44rem;height:auto;margin:.35rem 0 .15rem" aria-labelledby="e7-title e7-desc">
  <title id="e7-title">Density feedback — not automatic monopoly</title>
  <desc id="e7-desc">Density feedback loop: more flights on shared fixed cost such as pad rent lead to lower average cost per flight when utilization rises, which can strengthen position at that site if demand and permission hold. ### Scarce pads can soften price wars {#f02-bertrand}

Open in [Week 2 notes](week-02.qmd#w02-bertrand-svg).

```{=html}
<figure class="wdiag wdiag-svg" id="w02-bertrand-svg" aria-labelledby="w02-bertrand-svg-title">
<p class="wdiag-cap" id="w02-bertrand-svg-title"><strong>Scarce pads can soften price wars</strong> — with unconstrained capacity and a homogeneous product, Bertrand undercutting can push <em>P</em> toward <em>MC</em>. When pad rules leave <strong>total capacity below demand</strong>, neither firm can absorb the market by cutting price alone — scarcity <strong>may</strong> soften wars. Capacity limits do <strong>not</strong> guarantee high prices or profits. Classroom only (MC = HK$100; WTP up to HK$500; demand = 100).</p>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 720 300" role="img" style="display:block;width:100%;max-width:44rem;height:auto;margin:.35rem 0 .15rem" aria-labelledby="n2-title n2-desc">

Capacity limits do not guarantee high prices or profits. Classroom screen only. Sandbox is not Sandbox X. No invented corridor capacity.</desc>

### Revenue = seats × load factor × average fare — fill ≠ contribution {#f03-rm}

Open in [Week 3 notes](week-03.qmd#w03-rm-svg).

```{=html}
<figure class="wdiag wdiag-svg" id="w03-rm-svg" aria-labelledby="w03-rm-svg-title">
<p class="wdiag-cap" id="w03-rm-svg-title"><strong>Revenue = seats × load factor × average fare — fill ≠ contribution</strong> — revenue management improves <strong>total expected contribution</strong>, not merely empty-seat elimination. Maximising load factor alone is the wrong goal if fares collapse. High utilization that fills seats at wrecked fares can look good on a load-factor chart and still fail contribution. Cargo: payload × price per kg / mission — same idea, different unit.</p>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" style="display:block;width:100%;max-width:44rem;height:auto;margin:.35rem 0 .15rem" viewBox="0 0 720 340" role="img" aria-labelledby="p4-title p4-desc">

  <desc id="p4-desc">Passenger revenue equals seats times load factor times average fare. Maximising load factor alone is the wrong goal if fares collapse. Fill every seat can wreck contribution. For cargo use payload times price per kilogram or per mission. Sandbox is not Sandbox X.</desc>

### Breakeven volume {#f03-breakeven}

Open in [Week 3 notes](week-03.qmd#w03-breakeven-svg).

```{=html}
<figure class="wdiag wdiag-svg" id="w03-breakeven-svg" aria-labelledby="w03-breakeven-svg-title">
<p class="wdiag-cap" id="w03-breakeven-svg-title"><strong>Breakeven volume</strong> — breakeven units = fixed cost ÷ (revenue per unit − variable cost per unit). Denominator = <strong>contribution margin</strong> per unit. Daily form: required missions/day = fixed daily cost ÷ contribution margin per mission. Compare with capacity, hours, charging, weather, and demand — required activity is <strong>not</strong> an automatic traffic forecast. Classroom units only.</p>

Equivalently, required missions per day equal fixed daily cost divided by contribution margin per mission. Compare the target with physical capacity, hours, charging, weather and expected demand. Classroom units only.</desc>

### Taxi GC vs air — VOT HK$15/min {#f04-gc}

Open in [Week 4 notes](week-04.qmd#w04-gc-svg).

```{=html}
<figure class="wdiag wdiag-svg" id="w04-gc-svg" aria-labelledby="w04-gc-svg-title">
<p class="wdiag-cap" id="w04-gc-svg-title"><strong>Taxi GC vs air — VOT HK$15/min</strong> — Classroom: ground taxi fare <strong>HK$350</strong> · 45 min · other HK$50 → GC <strong>HK$1,075</strong>; air-mobility fare <strong>HK$800</strong> · 12 min · other HK$80 → GC <strong>HK$1,060</strong>. Air slightly preferred under these assumptions; a small wait / reliability / risk shift can reverse the ranking. GC ranks options for a traveller type — <strong>≠ mode share</strong>, elasticity, or revenue. Sandbox ≠ Sandbox X.</p>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" style="display:block;width:100%;max-width:44rem;height:auto;margin:.35rem 0 .15rem" viewBox="0 0 720 360" role="img" aria-labelledby="t2-title t2-desc">

  <desc id="t2-desc">Classroom generalized cost comparison at value of time fifteen Hong Kong dollars per minute. Ground taxi: fare three hundred fifty, door-to-door forty-five minutes, other burden fifty, GC one thousand seventy-five. Air-mobility service: fare eight hundred, door-to-door twelve minutes, other burden eighty, GC one thousand sixty. A small change in waiting, reliability, or perceived risk can reverse the ranking. Generalized cost ranks options for a traveller type; it does not by itself give mode share. Sandbox is not Sandbox X.</desc>

<p class="wdiag-cap" id="w04-elasticity-svg-title"><strong>Elasticity and a price cut</strong> — |E_d| &lt; 1 inelastic; |E_d| &gt; 1 elastic. <figure class="wdiag wdiag-svg" id="w05-site-screen-svg" aria-labelledby="w05-site-screen-svg-title">
<p class="wdiag-cap" id="w05-site-screen-svg-title"><strong>Site selection — five screens</strong> — safety/obstacles; customer access (Week 4 GC); utilities and operations; capacity and expandability; cost and approval. ### Daily infrastructure cost — HK$15k vs HK$4k {#f05-infra-cost}

Open in [Week 5 notes](week-05.qmd#w05-infra-cost-svg).

```{=html}
<figure class="wdiag wdiag-svg" id="w05-infra-cost-svg" aria-labelledby="w05-infra-cost-svg-title">
<p class="wdiag-cap" id="w05-infra-cost-svg-title"><strong>Daily infrastructure cost — HK$15k vs HK$4k</strong> — (CAPEX − residual) ÷ useful days + daily OPEX. Classroom: higher-investment CAPEX <strong>HK$18.25M</strong> → daily economic cost <strong>HK$15,000</strong>; lower-investment CAPEX <strong>HK$3.65M</strong> → <strong>HK$4,000</strong> (10-year life, no residual, 3,650 days). Higher-cost site must earn extra demand / price / reliability / network value. Unit-cost screen ≠ cash flow or NPV. Digital/data layers ≠ funded vertiport statute. Sandbox ≠ Sandbox X.</p>

### Scarce slots — four controls; revenue max ≠ goal {#f05-slots}

Open in [Week 5 notes](week-05.qmd#w05-slots-svg).

<figure class="wdiag wdiag-svg" id="w05-slots-svg" aria-labelledby="w05-slots-svg-title">
<p class="wdiag-cap" id="w05-slots-svg-title"><strong>Scarce slots — four controls; revenue max ≠ goal</strong> — administrative · market · priority · operational controls. Illustrative peak fee: base <strong>HK$100</strong> + congestion <strong>HK$200</strong> × (requests / slots) → <strong>2/2 → HK$300</strong>; <strong>8/2 → HK$900</strong>. Design choice, <strong>not</strong> a Hong Kong tariff. Revenue maximisation alone is <strong>not</strong> the goal of scarce infrastructure allocation. Sandbox / Sandbox X ≠ permanent commercial slot right. No invented corridor <em>K</em>.</p>

<p class="wdiag-cap" id="w05-network-topo-title"><strong>Hub, distributed, or hybrid — different GC stories</strong> — concentrated hub (shared facilities, longer access / single-site risk), distributed (better access and resilience; duplicated fixed cost), hybrid (hubs plus feeders; coordination complexity). GC per trip = (network cost bundle ÷ served trips) + access burden. Classroom check: concentrated ≈ HK$123.75 vs distributed ≈ HK$41.25 at 4,000 served trips/day — ranking can reverse. No universal Hong Kong or GBA template.</p>

### Who bears demand risk? {#f06-pay}

Open in [Week 6 notes](week-06.qmd#w06-pay-svg).

```{=html}
<figure class="wdiag wdiag-text" id="f06-pay-text" aria-labelledby="f06-pay-text-title">
<details class="wdiag-text-details">
<summary class="wdiag-text-sum">Text diagram</summary>
<p class="wdiag-cap" id="f06-pay-text-title"><strong>Who bears demand risk?</strong></p>
<div class="wdiag-stack cols-2">
<div class="wdiag-box"><strong>Usage payment</strong><br/>Cash follows traffic / missions → operator (or SPV) bears more demand risk.</div>
<div class="wdiag-box"><strong>Availability payment</strong><br/>Cash follows agreed readiness / service level → public sponsor often bears more demand risk.</div>
</div>
<p class="wdiag-arrow" aria-hidden="true">↕ hybrids exist</p>
<div class="wdiag-box fact"><strong>Write the risk down</strong><br/>Payment design is a risk allocation, not a slogan.</div>
<p class="wdiag-note">Classroom payment figures are illustrative — not CAD or government tariffs.</p>
</details>
</figure>
```

```{=html}
<figure class="wdiag wdiag-svg" id="w06-pay-svg" aria-labelledby="w06-pay-svg-title">
<p class="wdiag-cap" id="w06-pay-svg-title"><strong>Who bears demand risk?</strong> — Usage payment: cash follows traffic / missions → operator (or SPV) bears more demand risk. Availability payment: cash follows agreed readiness / service level → public sponsor often bears more demand risk; provider keeps performance risk via KPIs and deductions. Hybrids exist. Availability pays for readiness — not a free weather hedge. Classroom figures only — not CAD tariffs. Keep Sandbox ≠ Sandbox X.</p>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 720 400" role="img" style="display:block;width:100%;max-width:44rem;height:auto;margin:.35rem 0 .15rem" aria-labelledby="c10-title c10-desc">
  <title id="c10-title">Who bears demand risk?</title>
  <desc id="c10-desc">Two payment designs. Usage payment: cash follows traffic or missions, so the operator or SPV bears more demand risk. Availability payment: cash follows agreed readiness or service level, so the public sponsor often bears more demand risk while the provider keeps performance risk through KPIs and deductions. An arrow notes hybrids exist. Availability pays for readiness, not a free weather hedge.</desc>
  <rect x="12" y="12" width="696" height="376" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#d9d4c7" stroke-width="1"/>
  <text x="360" y="36" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui,Segoe UI,sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="700" fill="#003366">Who bears demand risk?</text>

### Net readiness · lead ≠ monopoly {#f07-readiness}

Open in [Week 7 notes](week-07.qmd#w07-readiness-svg).

```{=html}
<figure class="wdiag wdiag-svg" id="w07-readiness-svg" aria-labelledby="w07-readiness-svg-title">
<p class="wdiag-cap" id="w07-readiness-svg-title"><strong>Net readiness · lead ≠ monopoly</strong> — Classroom: monthly contribution after approval <strong>HK$2M</strong>; additional compliance <strong>HK$15M</strong>. <strong>12-month</strong> lead: 12×2 = HK$24M − 15 → net <strong>HK$9M</strong>. <strong>6-month</strong> lead: 6×2 = HK$12M − 15 → net <strong>−HK$3M</strong>. Early readiness has value only if the lead is long enough and commercially useful — not monopoly protection. Approval ≠ franchise. Readiness ≠ Sandbox selection (38/72). Sandbox ≠ Sandbox X. U-space ≠ HK law.</p>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" style="display:block;width:100%;max-width:44rem;height:auto;margin:.35rem 0 .15rem" viewBox="0 0 720 360" role="img" aria-labelledby="v1-title v1-desc">
  <title id="v1-title">Net readiness value: twelve-month lead nine million versus six-month lead minus three million</title>
  <desc id="v1-desc">Classroom readiness. Monthly contribution after approval two million Hong Kong dollars. Additional compliance cost fifteen million. Twelve-month lead: contribution twenty-four million minus fifteen million equals net nine million. Six-month lead: contribution twelve million minus fifteen million equals net minus three million. Early readiness has value only if the lead is long enough and commercially useful. It does not imply monopoly protection. Approval is not a franchise. Readiness is not Sandbox selection thirty-eight of seventy-two. Sandbox is not Sandbox X. U-space is not Hong Kong law.</desc>

### Congestion cost is what you impose on others {#f08-mcc}

Open in [Week 8 notes](week-08.qmd#w08-mcc-svg).

```{=html}
<figure class="wdiag wdiag-svg" id="w08-mcc-svg" aria-labelledby="w08-mcc-svg-title">
<p class="wdiag-cap" id="w08-mcc-svg-title"><strong>Congestion cost is what you impose on others</strong> — marginal congestion cost sums additional delay × value of delay across affected users, then adds other incremental costs (MCC). Pricing is only one response; reservations, quotas, priority rules, rerouting, and capacity investment may also fit. Some public-service missions need <strong>explicit priority</strong> rather than willingness to pay. Classroom delay screens only — not published CAD capacities; do not invent corridor <em>K</em>.</p>

### Profit is not social net benefit {#f09-two-lenses}

Open in [Week 9 notes](week-09.qmd#w09-two-lenses).

```{=html}
<figure class="wdiag wdiag-svg" id="w09-two-lenses" aria-labelledby="w09-two-lenses-title">
<p class="wdiag-cap" id="w09-two-lenses-title"><strong>Profit is not social net benefit</strong> — commercial lens: can the operator cover variable cost (then fixed cost)? Social lens: do total gains exceed total costs for society, including externalities and who gains or bears burdens? A profitable service can still create social costs; an unprofitable service may create important public benefits.</p>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 720 390" role="img" style="display:block;width:100%;max-width:44rem;height:auto;margin:.35rem 0 .15rem" aria-labelledby="d3-title d3-desc">
  <title id="d3-title">Profit is not social net benefit</title>
  <desc id="d3-desc">Two appraisal lenses. Commercial contribution margin asks whether the operator can cover variable cost and then fixed cost. Social benefit-cost asks whether total gains exceed total costs for society, including externalities and distribution. A profitable service can still create social costs; an unprofitable service may create important public benefits.</desc>
  <rect x="12" y="12" width="696" height="366" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#d9d4c7" stroke-width="1"/>

  <text x="190" y="168" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui,Segoe UI,sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="700" fill="#003366">Can the operator cover</text>

  <rect x="380" y="78" width="300" height="200" rx="8" fill="#F7F6F3" stroke="#d9d4c7"/>
  <text x="530" y="108" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui,Segoe UI,sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="700" fill="#003366">Social lens</text>

  <text x="530" y="168" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui,Segoe UI,sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="700" fill="#003366">Do total gains exceed</text>

### Uncertainty — scenarios and expected value {#f09-uncertainty}

Open in [Week 9 notes](week-09.qmd#w09-uncertainty-svg).

```{=html}
<figure class="wdiag wdiag-svg" id="w09-uncertainty-svg" aria-labelledby="w09-uncertainty-svg-title">
<p class="wdiag-cap" id="w09-uncertainty-svg-title"><strong>Uncertainty — scenarios and expected value</strong> — use base, downside, and upside (plus sensitivity / ranges where justified). $E[\Pi]=\sum_s \Pr(s)\,\Pi_s$. Monte Carlo shows a <strong>distribution of outcomes</strong> — it does <strong>not</strong> make weak assumptions accurate; it makes their implications visible. Also check probability of loss and downside cash needs. Classroom numbers illustrative.</p>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 720 330" role="img" style="display:block;width:100%;max-width:44rem;height:auto;margin:.35rem 0 .15rem" aria-labelledby="j5-title j5-desc">
  <title id="j5-title">Uncertainty — scenarios and expected value</title>
  <desc id="j5-desc">Use a base case, downside and upside scenarios, sensitivity analysis, and probability ranges where justified. Monte Carlo simulation samples uncertain inputs and recalculates the model to show a distribution of outcomes. Simulation does not make weak assumptions accurate; it makes their implications visible. Expected profit equals the sum over scenarios of probability times profit. Also look at probability of loss and downside cash needs.</desc>
  <rect x="12" y="12" width="696" height="306" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#d9d4c7" stroke-width="1"/>

  <text x="360" y="52" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui,Segoe UI,sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#5f5f5f">Make weak assumptions visible — do not pretend they are accurate</text>

  <text x="360" y="104" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui,Segoe UI,sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#003366">Downside</text>

  <text x="360" y="214" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui,Segoe UI,sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="700" fill="#ffffff">E[Π] = Σ Pr(s) × Π_s</text>

### Scopes vs LCA — different questions {#f10-ghg}

Open in [Week 10 notes](week-10.qmd#w10-ghg-svg).

```{=html}
<figure class="wdiag wdiag-text" id="f10-ghg-text" aria-labelledby="f10-ghg-text-title">
<details class="wdiag-text-details">
<summary class="wdiag-text-sum">Text diagram</summary>
<p class="wdiag-cap" id="f10-ghg-text-title"><strong>Scopes vs LCA (different questions)</strong></p>
<div class="wdiag-stack cols-2">
<div class="wdiag-box"><strong>Corporate scopes 1–3</strong><br/>Organisation boundary: direct, purchased energy, other value-chain.</div>
<div class="wdiag-box"><strong>Product / service LCA</strong><br/>Functional unit across a defined life cycle (vehicle, battery, infra, ops, end-of-life).</div>
</div>
<div class="wdiag-box fact" style="margin-top:.35rem"><strong>Electric ≠ zero life-cycle emissions</strong><br/>Match boundaries before comparing modes. Do not add scopes to LCA totals without a map.</div>
<p class="wdiag-note">Use sourced grid factors for real inventories; classroom kWh factors are illustrative.</p>
</details>
</figure>
```

```{=html}
<figure class="wdiag wdiag-svg" id="w10-ghg-svg" aria-labelledby="w10-ghg-svg-title">
<p class="wdiag-cap" id="w10-ghg-svg-title"><strong>Scopes vs LCA — different questions</strong> — corporate Scopes 1–3 use an organisation boundary; product/service LCA uses a functional unit across vehicle, battery, infrastructure, operations, and end-of-life. <strong>Electric ≠ zero life-cycle emissions.</strong> Do not add Scope totals to an LCA total without a boundary map. Classroom kWh factors are illustrative.</p>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 720 380" role="img" style="display:block;width:100%;max-width:44rem;height:auto;margin:.35rem 0 .15rem" aria-labelledby="d4-title d4-desc">

Do not add scopes totals to an LCA total without a boundary map.</desc>

```{=html}
<figure class="wdiag wdiag-svg" id="w10-fund-ps-svg" aria-labelledby="w10-fund-ps-svg-title">

Classroom: <strong>100</strong> daily slots; commercial <strong>HK$400</strong>/flight; public-service incremental <strong>HK$100</strong>/flight; <strong>20</strong> priority slots cost ~<strong>HK$10k/day</strong> opportunity vs all-commercial. Public-service payment must be a transparent source. Sandbox is not Sandbox X.</desc>

### Capacity shock · K binds → Π → 0 {#f11-cap-shock}

Open in [Week 11 notes](week-11.qmd#w11-cap-shock-svg).

```{=html}
<figure class="wdiag wdiag-svg" id="w11-cap-shock-svg" aria-labelledby="w11-cap-shock-svg-title">
<p class="wdiag-cap" id="w11-cap-shock-svg-title"><strong>Capacity shock · K binds → Π → 0</strong> — Classroom: <em>D</em>=100 flights/day; <em>p</em>=600; <em>v</em>=100; <em>F</em>=HK$40,000/day. Base <em>K</em>=100 → min{100,100}=100 → Π = <strong>HK$10,000/day</strong>. Shock <em>K</em>=80 → min{100,80}=80 → Π = <strong>HK$0/day</strong>. Same demand; fixed cost remains. Raising marketing to lift <em>D</em> does nothing when <em>K</em> binds. Illustrative — not Hong Kong weather downtime. Sandbox ≠ Sandbox X. No invented corridor <em>K</em>.</p>

Same demand; K binds. Illustrative — not Hong Kong weather downtime. Sandbox is not Sandbox X. No invented corridor capacity.</desc>

  <title id="a6-title">Count links: five nodes yield six candidates; twenty nodes about twenty-nine after screening</title>

### Five-step exam method {#f12-exam}

```{=html}

<details class="wdiag-text-details">
<summary class="wdiag-text-sum">Text diagram</summary>
<p class="wdiag-cap" id="f12-exam-text-title"><strong>Five-step exam method</strong></p>
<div class="wdiag-flow">
<div class="wdiag-box"><strong>1</strong> Define the decision &amp; alternative</div>
<div class="wdiag-arrow" aria-hidden="true">↓</div>
<div class="wdiag-box"><strong>2</strong> Served activity min{D, K}</div>
<div class="wdiag-arrow" aria-hidden="true">↓</div>
<div class="wdiag-box"><strong>3</strong> Viability (p, v, F, specified charges)</div>
<div class="wdiag-arrow" aria-hidden="true">↓</div>
<div class="wdiag-box"><strong>4</strong> Map each constraint once</div>
<div class="wdiag-arrow" aria-hidden="true">↓</div>
<div class="wdiag-box fact"><strong>5</strong> Recommend conditionally (proceed / pause / redesign / stop)</div>
</div>

```{=html}
